t: How is the End of Service Benefit calculated? What is the formula?
b: EOS = completed years of service (no fractions) x last drawn basic salary x multiplier. The multiplier is 1.0 for 5 to 10 years, 1.25 for 10 to 15 years, and 1.5 for 15 years and above. Example: 12 completed years with a basic salary of BDT 50,000 would be 50,000 x 1.25 x 12 = BDT 750,000, before tax. Income tax due on the benefit is paid by the employee and adjusted in the final payment (amendment effective 1 July 2024). Note that 10 and 15 years sit in two bands, so confirm the exact boundary case with HR.
src: HR Policy: End of Service Benefit Policy (v01, effective 1 Jan 2024; amended 4 Sep 2024)

t: Does the company pay the tax on the End of Service Benefit?
b: No, not since 1 July 2024. The amendment of 4 September 2024 removed the earlier 'grossing up withholding tax' wording. Any applicable income tax on the EOS Benefit is payable by the employee and is adjusted with the final payment. Before that date the policy said the benefit was calculated including grossing up the withholding tax.
src: HR Policy: End of Service Benefit Policy (v01, effective 1 Jan 2024; amended 4 Sep 2024)

t: Is EOS Benefit the same as Gratuity? What happened to the Gratuity policy?
b: EOS Benefit replaced Gratuity. The Board approved 'End of Service Benefit' in lieu of 'Gratuity' in November 2023, the Gratuity policy circulated on 9 July 2023 was cancelled, and the EOS policy took effect on 1 January 2024.
src: HR Policy: End of Service Benefit Policy (v01, effective 1 Jan 2024; amended 4 Sep 2024)

t: Do warnings or disciplinary action affect my End of Service Benefit?
b: Yes. If an employee receives 2 warning letters, or any other disciplinary punishment approved by the Managing Director (increment hold, downgradation, fine and so on), in a year, that year is not counted for EOS. An unsatisfactory performance rating in a year has the same effect. Example from the policy: an employee with 5 years who falls under this rule in one year is paid basic x 1.0 x 4. Dismissal or a criminal conviction removes eligibility altogether.
src: HR Policy: End of Service Benefit Policy (v01, effective 1 Jan 2024; amended 4 Sep 2024)

t: Performance Appraisal Policy: purpose, scope and process
b:
Policy: Performance Appraisal Policy, version 01, owner HR, effective 1 June 2025.
Purpose: to achieve company objectives through a clear and consistent framework for evaluating employee, departmental and organizational performance, so that employees are rightly evaluated (from high performer to non-performer) and rewarded or reprised accordingly.
Scope: all confirmed permanent employees, and any group the management includes in the Annual Performance Appraisal (APA).
Process (clause 4): (1) set organizational, departmental and individual objectives and KPIs, as detailed in the KPI Based Performance Management Policy (effective 1 August 2023); (2) conduct monthly, quarterly, half-yearly and yearly evaluations; (3) take action for non-performers under the Reward and Reprisal Policy (effective 1 August 2023); (4) conduct the Annual Performance Appraisal. The Monthly Performance Evaluation (MPE) in Annexure 3 stays in effect until the KPI module is fully operational in HRIS.
Individual evaluation has two areas: (a) Objective & KPI evaluation and (b) 9 Box evaluation (future leadership assessment).
Management may modify, suspend or discontinue the policy at its sole discretion.
src: HR Policy: Performance Appraisal Policy (v01, effective 1 Jun 2025)

t: Performance Appraisal: assessment frequency, grades and bell curve
b:
Assessment frequency:
- Individual quantitative (Objective & KPI): Executive and above, quarterly and yearly; below Executive, monthly and yearly.
- Individual qualitative (Core Values & Core Competencies): half-yearly and yearly.
- Individual 9 Box (future leadership): half-yearly and yearly.
- Departmental assessment: quarterly and yearly. Organizational assessment: half-yearly and yearly.
Performance grade and limit:
- Exceptional: above 100%, bell curve limit 10% to 15%.
- Strong: above 90% up to 100%, 15% to 20%. (Exceptional plus Strong: maximum 35%.)
- Satisfactory: 70% to 90% inclusive, 60% to 65% (the rest).
- Needs Improvement: below 70%, 5% to 10% (minimum 5%).
Note 1: if a department does not mark at least 5% as 'Needs Improvement', the lowest 5% of evaluated employees are treated as 'Needs Improvement', and the same method applies to the other grades.
Note 2: a formal performance dialogue between the employee and the line manager must take place in each quarter's evaluation.
Caution: the 2023 KPI Based PMS policy shows a bell curve for the qualitative score with Strong 60-65% and Satisfactory 15-20%; the 2025 Appraisal Policy gives Strong 15-20% and Satisfactory 60-65%. The later (2025) policy is the one to apply; confirm with HR.
src: HR Policy: Performance Appraisal Policy (v01, effective 1 Jun 2025)

t: Performance Appraisal: 9 Box evaluation (future leadership assessment)
b:
The 9 Box Model assesses future leaders. Past Performance (horizontal axis) is the individual quantitative KPI achievement score (out of 70). Growth Potential (vertical axis) is the individual qualitative score of Core Values & Core Competencies (out of 30). Scale for each axis: High above 90%; Moderate 70% to 90%; Low below 70%.
Boxes (performance / potential): Rough Diamond (low/high), Future Star (moderate/high), Consistent Star (high/high), Inconsistent Player (low/moderate), Key Player (moderate/moderate), Current Star (high/moderate), Talent Risk (low/low), Solid Professional (moderate/low), High Professional (high/low).
Groups, score on each axis and bell curve:
- Future Potential Leaders (Consistent Star, Future Star, Current Star): above 80%, top 10% to 15%.
- Performance Enhancement Group (Key Player, Rough Diamond, High Professional): above 80%, next 15% to 20%. Together these two groups are a maximum of 35%.
- Performance Improvement Group (Inconsistent Player, Solid Professional): 70% or higher, 60% to 65% (the rest).
- Talent Risk Group (Talent Risk): below 70%, 5% to 10% (minimum 5%). The action plan for this box is shown as 'Discontinuation (Talent Risk)'.
src: HR Policy: Performance Appraisal Policy (v01, effective 1 Jun 2025)

t: Performance Appraisal: promotion and upgradation criteria and level matrix
b:
'Promotion' is an elevation with a new scope of role and new responsibilities. 'Upgradation' is an elevation within the same role with higher responsibility.
Level matrix. Management group: Promotion applies for Director to CXO, Sr. GM to Director, GM to Sr. GM, DGM to GM, AGM to DGM, Sr. Manager to AGM, Manager to Sr. Manager, Dy. Manager to Manager, Sr. Executive to Asst. Manager and Sr. Associate Executive to Executive. Upgradation applies for Asst. Manager to Dy. Manager, Executive to Sr. Executive and Associate Executive to Sr. Associate Executive. CXO is at management discretion. Technician group: Promotion for Sr. Technician to Chief Technician, Technician to Sr. Technician and Asst. Technician to Technician; Upgradation for Jr. Technician to Asst. Technician; Chief Technician N/A. General group: Promotion for General II to General I; Upgradation for General III to General II; General I N/A.
All of the following criteria must be met (Promotion / Upgradation):
1. A vacancy as per the approved organogram (both).
2. Minimum length of service in the current position: 3 years / 2 years.
3. Individual performance (quantitative + qualitative): above 90% / minimum 85%.
4. Promotion/Upgradation evaluation (written, presentation, viva): minimum 75% (both).
5. 9 Box result: Future Potential Leaders (both).
6. Not more than one warning letter or other disciplinary action since the last APA (both).
Notes: top eligible candidates are ranked by the total of individual performance marks and evaluation marks. An employee rated 'Exceptional' who is also a 'Consistent Star' in the 9 Box in 2 consecutive years is eligible for promotion.
src: HR Policy: Performance Appraisal Policy (v01, effective 1 Jun 2025)

t: Performance Appraisal: promotion assessment (written test, presentation, viva)
b:
Held in the 4th quarter. Employees who meet criteria 2, 3 and 6 (service length, performance, discipline) are eligible.
Weights by present level: Director, Sr. GM, GM, DGM: recommended by HODs and finalized by the MD and Chairman. AGM, Sr. Manager, Manager: presentation 40%, viva 60%. Deputy Manager, Asst. Manager, Sr. Executive: written 20%, presentation 30%, viva 50%. Executive, Sr. Associate Executive, Associate Executive: written 40%, viva 60%. Technician and General groups: viva 100%.
Written test (2 hours, 100 marks): Business & Organization Knowledge 50, Situation based evaluation 30, Analytical and IQ 20.
Presentation (50 marks; 15 minutes: 10 minutes presentation and 5 minutes questions): based on self objective/KPI achievement and 3 new ideas on cost minimization and process efficiency. Marks: introduction 5; coverage of the subject 10; knowledge on subject 10; communication skills 10; punctuality 5; questions and answers 10.
Viva (50 marks, 15 to 20 minutes): five F@H core competencies 20 (Service Excellence, Agility, Process-compliance-cost efficiency, Professional Expertise, Security); Emotional Intelligence and Resilience 10; Leadership & Behavioral Competency 10; Business Knowledge 10.
Qualifying marks: written 60%, presentation 70%, viva 75%. The panel average is the final mark for presentation and viva.
Viva board: AGM to DGM and Sr. Manager to AGM: president 1 CXO, members 2 CXOs. Manager to Sr. Manager, Deputy Manager to Manager, Asst. Manager to Deputy Manager: president 1 CXO, members 1 CXO/Director and 1 Sr. GM/GM. Sr. Executive to Asst. Manager and Executive to Sr. Executive: president 1 CXO/Director, members 2 Sr. GM/GM/DGM. Sr. Associate Executive to Executive and Associate Executive to Sr. Associate Executive: president 1 Sr. GM/GM, members 2 GM/DGM/AGM. Below Executive (Technician and General groups): president 1 DGM/AGM, members 2 Sr. Manager/Manager. Levels from DGM upward: board recommended by HODs and finalized by the MD and Chairman.
Process: the department proposes promotions based on vacancies (maximum 3 employees per vacancy); HR reviews against the criteria and reports to management; the final decision is made with the MD and the respective HODs.
src: HR Policy: Performance Appraisal Policy (v01, effective 1 Jun 2025)

t: Performance Appraisal: increment guideline
b:
Individual Increment Factor weights: for Manager and above, Company objective/KPI 30%, Departmental objective/KPI 30%, Individual performance 40%. For below Manager: 20%, 20% and 60%.
Total yearly increment budget is fixed with management; a level-wise maximum budget is allocated from it. Individual increment = Individual Increment Factor x level-wise increment budget.
Individual increment factor by performance score: below 70: 0%; 70-75: 75%; 76-80: 80%; 81-85: 85%; 86-90: 90%; 91-95: 95%; 96-100: 100%; above 100: proportionate.
Other rules: outlier employees are kept within 10%, and any budget adjustment is made with the MD. Promoted or upgraded employees get an additional increment set every year within the total budget. All confirmed employees with at least 6 months of service are eligible. For first-time increment, the increment budget factor is 120% for 15 months and above, 100% for 9 to 15 months and 80% for 6 to 9 months of service. The increment exercise is completed within the 1st quarter of the next appraisal year. Increment is based solely on organizational, departmental and individual performance scores; no departmental feedback is collected on the increment file.
src: HR Policy: Performance Appraisal Policy (v01, effective 1 Jun 2025)

t: Monthly Performance Evaluation (MPE) in HRIS: deadlines
b:
Annexure 3 of the Performance Appraisal Policy. Associate Executive and above (excluding HODs) complete the Monthly Performance Evaluation in HRIS for the quantitative (KPI) part only, on a calendar-month cycle. Only the first line manager approves each month; HOF and HOD approval is not needed for MPE. HR downloads consolidated reports every quarter; the quarterly quantitative part (70%) goes to HOFs and HODs for review and final scoring. The qualitative part (Core Values and Core Competencies, 30%) is evaluated half-yearly with HOF and HOD approval. Path in HRIS: HRIS / MPE / MPE Form.
Deadlines: the employee submits monthly performance data by the 15th of the following month and the line manager approves by the 22nd (for example, January 2026 data is submitted by 15 February 2026 and approved by 22 February 2026). Non-compliance may affect monthly salary processing as per earlier practice.
src: HR Policy: Performance Appraisal Policy (v01, effective 1 Jun 2025)

t: What are the performance grades and their bell curve limits?
b: Under the 2025 Performance Appraisal Policy: Exceptional is above 100% (10% to 15% of employees); Strong is above 90% to 100% (15% to 20%); Satisfactory is 70% to 90% (60% to 65%); Needs Improvement is below 70% (5% to 10%, minimum 5%). Exceptional plus Strong may not exceed 35%. If a department does not mark at least 5% as Needs Improvement, its lowest 5% are treated as Needs Improvement.
src: HR Policy: Performance Appraisal Policy (v01, effective 1 Jun 2025)

t: What is needed to get promoted at Fiber@Home?
b: All six criteria must be met: a vacancy in the approved organogram; at least 3 years in the current position (2 years for upgradation); individual performance above 90% (minimum 85% for upgradation); at least 75% in the promotion evaluation (written, presentation, viva); a 9 Box result of Future Potential Leaders; and not more than one warning letter or other disciplinary action since the last appraisal. Qualifying marks are 60% for the written test, 70% for the presentation and 75% for the viva. Employees rated Exceptional and Consistent Star for 2 consecutive years are also eligible. A department may recommend up to 3 employees per vacancy.
src: HR Policy: Performance Appraisal Policy (v01, effective 1 Jun 2025)

t: How is the annual increment calculated?
b: Individual increment = Individual Increment Factor x the level-wise increment budget. The factor combines company, departmental and individual scores (30/30/40 for Manager and above; 20/20/60 below Manager) and is then scaled by the performance score: 0% below 70, 75% for 70-75, 80% for 76-80, 85% for 81-85, 90% for 86-90, 95% for 91-95, 100% for 96-100 and proportionate above 100. Confirmed employees with at least 6 months of service are eligible; the increment exercise finishes within the 1st quarter of the next appraisal year.
src: HR Policy: Performance Appraisal Policy (v01, effective 1 Jun 2025)

t: Who is eligible for an increment, and what applies to a first-time increment?
b: All confirmed employees with at least 6 months of service. For the first increment the budget factor depends on length of service: 80% for 6 to 9 months, 100% for 9 to 15 months and 120% for 15 months and above.
src: HR Policy: Performance Appraisal Policy (v01, effective 1 Jun 2025)

t: What is the 9 Box model and what are the Talent Risk and Future Star groups?
b: The 9 Box Model rates past performance (KPI score) against growth potential (core values and competencies score). Future Potential Leaders are Consistent Star, Future Star and Current Star (above 80% on each axis, top 10% to 15%). Talent Risk (below 70% on both, 5% to 10% of employees) is the lowest box and its action plan is shown as discontinuation. In between are the Performance Enhancement Group (Key Player, Rough Diamond, High Professional) and the Performance Improvement Group (Inconsistent Player, Solid Professional).
src: HR Policy: Performance Appraisal Policy (v01, effective 1 Jun 2025)

t: What is the deadline to submit the monthly performance evaluation (MPE) in HRIS?
b: Employees submit the previous month's data in HRIS by the 15th of the following month. The line manager approves by the 22nd. Late submission can affect monthly salary processing.
src: HR Policy: Performance Appraisal Policy (v01, effective 1 Jun 2025)

t: KPI Based Performance Management System: scope, weights and rating scale
b:
Version 1.01, effective 1 August 2023. Purpose: a robust Key Performance Indicator (KPI) based Performance Management System (PMS), aligning employee performance with functional, departmental and organizational objectives.
Scope: associate executive and above. Employees below executive are assessed by department-defined performance parameters. Evaluation cycle: July to June.
Weights: Quantitative 70% = Key Performance Indicators, assessed quarterly. Qualitative 30% = Core Values behavioral indicators 10% plus Core Competency behavioral indicators 20%, assessed half-yearly.
The KPI achievement score is to be generated automatically from integrated software; until integration is complete, supervisors validate it. A KPI Audit team formed by the Managing Director randomly checks KPI scores every quarter.
Rating scale: 4 Exceptional above 100%; 3 Strong above 90% to 100%; 2 Satisfactory above 70% to 90%; 1 Needs Improvement below 70%.
Qualitative scores are given by supervisors within a quota on a bell curve: Exceptional 10-15%, Strong 60-65%, Satisfactory 15-20%, Needs Improvement 5-10% (the later 2025 Performance Appraisal Policy swaps the Strong and Satisfactory ranges to 15-20% and 60-65%).
Future leaders are assessed with the 9 Box Model half-yearly and annually. The PMS lifecycle follows the yearly plan in Annexure 01. Monthly performance evaluation is discontinued by this policy (the 2025 appraisal policy keeps the MPE in HRIS until the KPI module is ready).
src: HR Policy: KPI Based Performance Management Policy (v1.01, effective 1 Aug 2023)
r: Sections: Purpose, Scope, Weights, Rating Scale

t: KPI PMS: quarterly performance presentation, performance dialogue and annexures
b:
Performance presentation is held quarterly in sequence: individuals present to their immediate supervisors, Heads of Function present to Heads of Department, and Heads of Department present departmental performance to the Chairman and Managing Director.
A formal performance dialogue is held twice a year between supervisors and team members, documented, with a 30-minute slot per team member. The Johari Window (Annexure 02) and the GROW coaching model (Annexure 03) are the frameworks. The GROW worksheet covers Goal, Reality, Obstacles, Options and Way Forward/Will.
The policy is effective from 1 August 2023 and may be modified by management as business needs require. Proposed by Md. Mahmudul Hasan (Manager, HR), recommended by Md. Masud Rabbi (Chief Human Resources Officer), approved by the Managing Director.
src: HR Policy: KPI Based Performance Management Policy (v1.01, effective 1 Aug 2023)
r: Sections: Presentation and Dialogue, Review of Policy

t: How is performance evaluated under the KPI Based PMS? What are the weights?
b: 70% is quantitative (KPI achievement, assessed quarterly) and 30% is qualitative: 10% for core values and 20% for core competency behavioral indicators, assessed half-yearly. It applies to associate executive and above; the cycle runs from July to June. Grades: Exceptional above 100%, Strong above 90% to 100%, Satisfactory above 70% to 90%, Needs Improvement below 70%.
src: HR Policy: KPI Based Performance Management Policy (v1.01, effective 1 Aug 2023)

t: What is KPI and PMS, and who does the KPI PMS apply to?
b: KPI means Key Performance Indicator and PMS means Performance Management System. At Fiber@Home the KPI Based PMS applies to associate executive and above designations. Employees below executive are assessed on department-defined performance parameters.
src: HR Policy: KPI Based Performance Management Policy (v1.01, effective 1 Aug 2023)

t: How often is there a performance dialogue between a manager and an employee?
b: The KPI policy requires a formal, documented performance dialogue twice a year (biannually), 30 minutes per team member, using the Johari Window and GROW model. The 2025 Performance Appraisal Policy additionally requires a formal dialogue between the employee and line manager in every quarterly evaluation.
src: HR Policy: KPI Based Performance Management Policy (v1.01, effective 1 Aug 2023)

t: Dress Code Policy: objective, scope and attire categories
b:
Policy No F@H/HR Policy/001, version 1.0, dated 10 September 2013, implemented from 15 September 2013. Objective: keep appearance consistent with the professional image of Fiber@Home; clothing, hairstyle and jewelry must not interfere with duties, and staff with customer contact must keep a suitable appearance.
Scope: all employees except those on field jobs, who dress appropriately for comfort and safety.
Formal Business Attire (meetings with clients, vendors or customers, in or outside the office): Men: formal trousers (no gabardine), suits with tie, formal coloured collared full/half sleeve shirt with or without tie, shoes. Women: salwar kameez, suits, saree, kurta/fotua, trousers with shirt, formal shoes or sandals.
Smart Casual: presentable, decent attire; suits, jackets and ties not mandatory. Allowed on all weekdays except meetings with outsiders (formal is required) and allowed for internal meetings. Effective 19 February 2024, 'jeans pant with shirt' was added to Smart Casual (HR notice of 16 October 2024).
Casual: only on Thursdays. Jeans trousers and polo shirts (with collar, half sleeves) may be worn while keeping the other guidelines.
src: HR Policy: Dress Code Policy (v1.0, dated 10 Sep 2013, implemented 15 Sep 2013)

t: Dress Code Policy: inappropriate attire and general guidelines
b:
Inappropriate attire: T-shirts without collar; shirts with slogans, suggestive cartoons or drawings; athletic/sportswear; shorts; torn pants/jeans and baggy/cargo trousers; revealing attire such as tank tops, crop tops, off-the-shoulder tops or see-through clothes; loose footwear such as flip-flops and slippers; party/evening wear.
HR reminder (16 October 2024): sandals, Panjabi and round-neck T-shirts are strictly prohibited, even on Casual days.
General guidelines: male employees must be clean-shaved or well-trimmed; decent haircut; good hygiene and neatly ironed clothes; minimal jewelry; clean, polished, securely fitted footwear; moving around the office in flip-flops or slippers is strictly prohibited; ID card must be visible while on duty; festive attire (saree, Panjabi, fatua etc.) is allowed and encouraged only on the next working day of the Eids, Pohela Boishakh and Pohela Falgun; anyone wanting to wear religious dress notifies HR; drivers, peons, security guards and other general staff wear company dress where provided.
src: HR Policy: Dress Code Policy (v1.0, dated 10 Sep 2013, implemented 15 Sep 2013)

t: Dress Code Policy: non-compliance and disciplinary action
b:
First violation: verbal warning from the HOD or Head of HR. From the second violation of the same policy: a warning letter for each instance. After 3 such warning letters the case goes to management.
Management may then take any of these actions according to gravity: deduct up to 10% of basic salary for a month; deny or postpone promotion for 12 months; deny or postpone increment for the next 12 months; separation of employment.
src: HR Policy: Dress Code Policy (v1.0, dated 10 Sep 2013, implemented 15 Sep 2013)

t: Can I wear jeans to the office?
b: Yes, in two cases: on Thursdays (Casual day: jeans trousers with a collared polo shirt), and, since 19 February 2024, 'jeans pant with shirt' is part of Smart Casual on weekdays. Torn jeans are not allowed, and meetings with outsiders require formal attire. Round-neck T-shirts, sandals and Panjabi are prohibited even on Casual days.
src: HR Policy: Dress Code Policy (v1.0, dated 10 Sep 2013, implemented 15 Sep 2013)

t: What is the dress code on Thursday? What is casual day?
b: Casual attire is allowed only on Thursdays: jeans trousers and a polo shirt with collar (half sleeves allowed), while keeping all other guidelines. T-shirts without collar, sportswear, shorts, flip-flops, slippers and sandals are still not allowed.
src: HR Policy: Dress Code Policy (v1.0, dated 10 Sep 2013, implemented 15 Sep 2013)

t: What happens if I violate the dress code?
b: A verbal warning from the HOD or Head of HR for the first violation, then a warning letter for each repeat violation. After 3 warning letters the case is escalated to management, which may deduct up to 10% of one month's basic salary, deny or postpone promotion or increment for 12 months, or separate the employee.
src: HR Policy: Dress Code Policy (v1.0, dated 10 Sep 2013, implemented 15 Sep 2013)

t: What attire is not allowed in the office?
b: Collarless T-shirts, shirts with slogans or suggestive drawings, sportswear, shorts, torn pants or jeans, baggy or cargo trousers, tank tops, crop tops, off-the-shoulder or see-through clothing, flip-flops, slippers and loose footwear, and party or evening wear. HR also lists sandals and Panjabi as prohibited, even on Casual days (festive Panjabi is allowed on the next working day of Eid, Pohela Boishakh and Pohela Falgun).
src: HR Policy: Dress Code Policy (v1.0, dated 10 Sep 2013, implemented 15 Sep 2013)

t: When can I wear festive dress such as Panjabi or saree?
b: Festive attire (saree, Panjabi, fatua etc.) is allowed and encouraged only on the next working day of Eid, Pohela Boishakh and Pohela Falgun, while keeping other decorum.
src: HR Policy: Dress Code Policy (v1.0, dated 10 Sep 2013, implemented 15 Sep 2013)

t: Festival Bonus Policy (amended): eligibility and calculation
b:
Festival Bonus Policy version 2.0, owner HR, effective 1 September 2024 (Amendment of Festival Bonus Policy). Management pays the festival bonus twice a year, at Eid ul-Fitr and Eid ul-Azha.
Eligibility: all confirmed employees receive 100% of the festival bonus, equivalent to one basic salary. Contractual employees become eligible for a bonus of one basic salary after completing 180 days of continuous service.
Length of service calculation: eligibility is calculated considering the Eid date according to the government calendar, based on the bonus declaration date (the reference date).
The terms of the earlier Festival Bonus approval dated 16 September 2015 are null and void. Management may amend the policy at any time. Recommended by the Manager HR (Md. Mahmudul Hasan), verified by the CHRO (Md. Masud Rabbi) and CFO (Jasim Uddin), approved by the Managing Director.
The policy does not mention probationers, trainees or interns.
src: HR Policy: Festival Bonus Policy, amendment (v2.0, effective 1 Sep 2024)

t: How much is the festival bonus and when is it paid?
b: Confirmed employees get 100% of the festival bonus, equal to one basic salary, twice a year: at Eid ul-Fitr and Eid ul-Azha. The service period is checked against the Eid date in the government calendar, based on the bonus declaration date.
src: HR Policy: Festival Bonus Policy, amendment (v2.0, effective 1 Sep 2024)

t: Are contractual employees eligible for the festival bonus?
b: Yes, after completing 180 days of continuous service. They then receive one basic salary per festival, like confirmed employees. The policy does not state anything about probationers, trainees or interns; ask HR.
src: HR Policy: Festival Bonus Policy, amendment (v2.0, effective 1 Sep 2024)

t: Leave Policy: types of leave and entitlement table
b:
Leave Policy version 2.0, owner HR, effective 1 October 2017, approved by the Managing Director. Leave entitlement is calculated on the financial year (July to June) and taken with the approval of the concerned authority.
Types: casual, sick, annual, maternity, special leave and day off.
Entitlement (days per year, casual / sick / annual):
- Probation: 3* / 5* / 0.
- Confirmed: 10 / 14 / 21.
- Trainee or contract for 1 year: 10 / 14 / 0.
- Trainee or contract for 6 months: 5 / 7 / 0.
- Trainee or contract for 3 months: 3 / 4 / 0.
- Intern: 0 / 0 / 0.
* Given as credit, adjusted after confirmation.
Probation: leave is calculated from the date of joining on a prorata basis but can be availed only after confirmation. 3 days casual and 5 days sick leave may be approved as credit and debited after confirmation. For an emergency, extra leave of absence (maximum 7 days) is adjusted from the annual leave entitlement.
Casual leave cannot be carried forward and cannot be granted for more than 3 days at a time. (The policy says 'calendar year' for carry-forward although entitlement runs on the financial year.)
src: HR Policy: Leave Policy (v2.0, effective 1 Oct 2017; amended 2 Jan 2024 and 3 Sep 2024)

t: Leave Policy: sick leave and prolonged sickness (amended 3 Sep 2024)
b:
Sick leave (clause 2.1c). Original rule: a medical certificate from a registered doctor, hospital or clinic was needed for more than 3 days. Amended 3 September 2024: the certificate must be submitted to HRD for a minimum of 1 (one) day of sick leave; until then HR verification in HRIS is withheld. If more sick leave is needed after sick and annual leave are used up, the case goes to the Managing Director.
New clause 2.1(C/1), Prolonged Sickness:
(i) On-job accident: leave duration is 6 months for a permanent employee (contractual: until contract end or 6 months, whichever is lower). Adjusted from sick leave first (from 14 days), then up to 5 days of casual leave (50% of the 10 days). Salary: first 2 months 100% of total salary, next 2 months two-thirds, next 2 months one-third.
(ii) Personal sickness (disease or accident outside the job): 3 months for a permanent employee (contractual: contract end or 3 months, whichever is lower). Adjusted from sick leave, then earn leave, then up to 5 days of casual leave. Salary: first 1 month 100%, next 1 month two-thirds, next 1 month one-third.
After these adjustments, if the employee still cannot join, the matter goes to management for a decision on service continuation. An employee declared unfit by a doctor's certificate may be discharged on management approval. Effective immediately on approval (3 September 2024).
src: HR Policy: Leave Policy (v2.0, effective 1 Oct 2017; amended 2 Jan 2024 and 3 Sep 2024)

t: Leave Policy: annual leave, earn leave encashment (amended 2 Jan 2024)
b:
Original annual leave rule (2017): up to 10 unavailed days a year could be encashed or carried forward, at (one month basic salary / 30) x unused days (maximum 10). Only confirmed employees below Manager level with 1 year of service on 30 June were eligible, paid once in the 1st quarter of the fiscal year. Annual leave could accumulate up to 60 days; up to 30 days at a time on special ground, more than 30 days for pilgrimage or sickness.
Amendment, Note of Approval Ref F@H/NOA/HR/2023-24/20 (2 January 2024, effective 1 January 2024) of Leave Policy clause 2.1(D), 'Earn Leave Encashment':
1. Applies to all permanent confirmed employees after 1 year of service as permanent employee.
2. A maximum of 10 days of unused earn leave is carried forward each year.
3. A maximum of 60 days can accumulate from carry-forward balances.
4. Instead of yearly encashment, a maximum of 60 days of earn leave is encashed at the time of separation.
5. Calculation: (last drawn basic salary / 30) x actual unused earn leave (maximum 60 days).
6. A maximum of 30 days of annual leave can be taken at a time on special ground; more than 30 days only for pilgrimage and sickness.
7. A resigned employee cannot take more than 7 days of leave during the notice period.
Note: the amendment says 'Earn Leave'; the 2017 policy calls the same entitlement 'Annual Leave'. Under the 2017 policy, on any separation the employee got encashment of up to 30 days of unused annual leave.
src: HR Policy: Leave Policy (v2.0, effective 1 Oct 2017; amended 2 Jan 2024 and 3 Sep 2024)

t: Leave Policy: maternity leave, special leave, day off and business travel
b:
Maternity leave: confirmed female employees get 112 days with pay. The application needs a doctor's certificate not less than 3 months before the Expected Date of Delivery (EDD). Maximum 2 times during Fiber@Home service. It cannot be accumulated and must be taken in a row: 8 weeks before and 8 weeks after the EDD (the authority may allow work longer if she feels able). Employers must not assign arduous work, long standing or health-risking work if she is likely to deliver within 10 weeks or delivered within the preceding 10 weeks. Additional leave on a doctor's advice (earn leave, sick leave) may follow.
Special leave: with management approval, with full, partial or no pay, considered after all other leave is used.
Day off: if an employee works at least 8 hours on a holiday, weekend or festival leave, a replacement day off can be taken within 30 days of the alternative working. Training participants are not covered (facilitators and organizers may take it). Either day off or holiday allowance, not both. Attendance or outstation/business travel approval in HRIS is a prerequisite.
Outstation/Business travel: prior approval through HRIS is required; unapproved travel is treated as unauthorized absence.
src: HR Policy: Leave Policy (v2.0, effective 1 Oct 2017; amended 2 Jan 2024 and 3 Sep 2024)

t: Leave Policy: general guidelines, approval matrix and holiday prefix/suffix rule
b:
General guidelines (2.2): pre-approval is required for planned leave; annual leave must be requested at least 5 days before. If pre-approval is impossible in an emergency, notify the line manager, HOF or HOD and apply immediately on rejoining. The employee is responsible for getting leave approved: for unapproved leave in the payroll month (26th to 25th) salary is held temporarily and released with the next payroll after approval. Leave is applied category-wise; extra leave after a category is used up may merge annual leave with other categories. After all leave is used, the HOD may approve up to 15 days of leave without pay in a year. During leave employees must be reachable by phone and email, may be recalled in an emergency, and must notify stakeholders of absence and the delegated person.
Approval matrix: up to Sr. Executive: verified by HR, recommended by Line Manager, approved by Head of Function. Asst. Manager to Sr. Manager: verified by HR, recommended by Line Manager, approved by Head of Department. AGM and above: verified by HR, recommended by Line Manager and Head of Department, approved by the Managing Director. The Executive Assistant puts MD leave approvals through HRIS; salary is not held for pending MD approval if the application was submitted to the MD's office beforehand.
Prefix/suffix rule: leave may be taken before or after a holiday, for any leave type. The weekend is Friday and Saturday. Example: leave on a Thursday only deducts 1 day; leave on Thursday plus the following Sunday deducts 4 days (the weekend counts); a Wednesday public holiday plus Thursday leave deducts 2 days (the shorter side of the holiday is added as the same leave category); Sunday to Thursday leave deducts 7 days.
src: HR Policy: Leave Policy (v2.0, effective 1 Oct 2017; amended 2 Jan 2024 and 3 Sep 2024)

t: How many casual, sick and annual leave days do I get?
b: A confirmed employee gets 10 casual, 14 sick and 21 annual leave days per financial year (July to June). Probationers get 3 casual and 5 sick days as credit (adjusted after confirmation) and no annual leave. Trainees or contract staff for 1 year get 10 casual and 14 sick; for 6 months 5 and 7; for 3 months 3 and 4; none get annual leave. Interns get no leave.
src: HR Policy: Leave Policy (v2.0, effective 1 Oct 2017; amended 2 Jan 2024 and 3 Sep 2024)

t: Do I need a medical certificate for sick leave?
b: Yes. Since the 3 September 2024 amendment a medical certificate from a registered doctor, hospital or clinic must be submitted to HRD for a minimum of 1 day of sick leave (previously it was needed only for more than 3 days). HR verification in HRIS stays on hold until it is submitted.
src: HR Policy: Leave Policy (v2.0, effective 1 Oct 2017; amended 2 Jan 2024 and 3 Sep 2024)

t: What happens if I have a prolonged illness or an accident at work?
b: Prolonged sickness leave is up to 6 months for an on-job accident and up to 3 months for personal sickness (permanent employees; contractual staff up to contract end or the same limit, whichever is lower). Salary: on-job accident 100% for 2 months, two-thirds for 2 months, one-third for 2 months; personal sickness 100% for 1 month, two-thirds for 1 month, one-third for 1 month. Leave is first taken from sick leave (14 days), then, for personal sickness, earn leave, then up to 5 days of casual leave. If still unable to return, management decides on service continuation and an unfit employee may be discharged.
src: HR Policy: Leave Policy (v2.0, effective 1 Oct 2017; amended 2 Jan 2024 and 3 Sep 2024)

t: How long is maternity leave at Fiber@Home?
b: 112 days with pay for confirmed female employees, taken as 8 weeks before and 8 weeks after the expected delivery date. It is allowed a maximum of 2 times in the employee's Fiber@Home service. The application needs a doctor's certificate not less than 3 months before the EDD. Additional leave on a doctor's advice can follow from earn or sick leave.
src: HR Policy: Leave Policy (v2.0, effective 1 Oct 2017; amended 2 Jan 2024 and 3 Sep 2024)

t: How is unused earn leave (annual leave) encashed?
b: Since 1 January 2024 earn leave is not encashed every year. Up to 10 unused days carry forward each year, the balance can reach 60 days, and a maximum of 60 days is encashed at separation. Formula: (last drawn basic salary / 30) x unused earn leave days (maximum 60). It applies to permanent confirmed employees after 1 year of service as a permanent employee.
src: HR Policy: Leave Policy (v2.0, effective 1 Oct 2017; amended 2 Jan 2024 and 3 Sep 2024)

t: How many days can I take leave at a time, and how much notice is needed?
b: Casual leave cannot exceed 3 days at a time. Annual leave of up to 30 days can be taken at once on special ground; more than 30 days only for pilgrimage or sickness. Annual leave needs approval at least 5 days in advance. A resigned employee cannot take more than 7 days of leave during the notice period.
src: HR Policy: Leave Policy (v2.0, effective 1 Oct 2017; amended 2 Jan 2024 and 3 Sep 2024)

t: Who approves my leave?
b: Up to Sr. Executive: the Line Manager recommends and the Head of Function approves. Asst. Manager to Sr. Manager: the Line Manager recommends and the Head of Department approves. AGM and above: the Line Manager and Head of Department recommend and the Managing Director approves. HR verifies in all cases.
src: HR Policy: Leave Policy (v2.0, effective 1 Oct 2017; amended 2 Jan 2024 and 3 Sep 2024)

t: What happens to my salary if my leave is not approved?
b: For unapproved leave within the payroll month (26th to 25th) salary is held temporarily and released with the next payroll after approval. If you could not apply in time because of an accident or unavoidable situation, notify HR formally through your line manager with the HOD's concern for normal salary payment. Unapproved business travel counts as unauthorized absence.
src: HR Policy: Leave Policy (v2.0, effective 1 Oct 2017; amended 2 Jan 2024 and 3 Sep 2024)

t: Is there a day off for working on a holiday or weekend?
b: Yes. If you work at least 8 hours on a holiday, weekend or festival leave day in the company's interest, you can take a replacement day off within 30 days. You get either the day off or holiday allowance, not both, and attendance or outstation approval in HRIS is required.
src: HR Policy: Leave Policy (v2.0, effective 1 Oct 2017; amended 2 Jan 2024 and 3 Sep 2024)

t: Welfare Fund Management Policy: definitions and areas of assistance
b:
Fiber@Home Employees Welfare Fund Management Policy (Bangla title: ফাইবার@হোম কর্মকর্তা/কর্মচারী কল্যাণ তহবিল ব্যবস্থাপনা বিধিমালা), version 1.0, owner HR, effective 1 July 2021. The original document is in Bangla; this is an English summary.
Definitions: 'family' means spouse, children and dependants. 'Employee' means all members entitled to benefits under the Fiber@Home Limited Employees Profit Participation and Welfare Fund policy. 'Fund source' is the money deposited in the Welfare Fund under that policy, or donations from any organization or person. A Board of Trustees runs the fund.
Areas of assistance (clause 3): education; medical; deceased person; religious/social/cultural/sports; child day care; pandemic medical; flood, cyclone and natural disaster; personal loan; and any other welfare area the Board of Trustees considers.
Allocation by area (clause 4): education 20%, medical 20%, deceased 20%, religious/social/cultural/sports 5%, day care 5%, pandemic medical 20%, flood/cyclone/disaster 5%, personal loan 5%; total 100%. Money not used in an area can be used in the same area in the same or later years, or in another area, by Board decision. The Board may change the allocation as needed. The policy lists personal loan (ব্যক্তিগত লোন) as an area with 5% allocation but the document contains no detailed loan terms.

- Admission to a government technical education institute: 5,000

t: Welfare Fund: medical, death, day care, pandemic and disaster assistance
b:
Medical (3.2): for treatment of members or families with incurable disease, subject to Board approval. Not applicable to ordinary illness. Serious illness or fatal injury: up to BDT 50,000. If someone is seriously ill or fatally injured at the workplace or while on duty, under section 150 of the Bangladesh Labour Act the company bears the cost from its own fund. Caesarean delivery: up to BDT 20,000. The Board may pay the grant partly or fully in advance and may raise the maximum limit in cases of serious illness or incurable disease. Proper proof is required. (Medical benefits covered by the Group Medical Insurance can no longer be claimed from this fund from 1 January 2024.)
Death (3.3): after HR receives the news of the death of an employee, the Board may pay a one-time maximum BDT 1,00,000 (one lakh) to the nominee, successor or guardian. On the death of a family member of a member, BDT 15,000 one-time.
Religious, social, cultural, sports (3.4): annual picnic, annual tour, Boishakhi (Pohela Boishakh) programme, games and other creative activities; also funded from the company's own fund.
Day care (3.5): up to two children under 6 years, up to BDT 20,000 one-time per child; not applicable if the company runs a day-care centre. Under section 94 of the Bangladesh Labour Act, if 40 or more women are employed the company provides a suitable room for children under 6 at its own cost.
Pandemic (3.6): up to BDT 50,000 on actual bills. COVID-19 positive employees: home isolation or treatment up to BDT 15,000; hospital admission up to BDT 50,000; company-arranged isolation from the welfare fund at actual cost; antibody test up to BDT 5,000.
Flood, cyclone and natural disaster (3.7): food aid and house construction, up to BDT 50,000; the Board may ask for a recommendation from the local chairman or member.

t: Welfare Fund: how to apply, time limit and approval
b:
Application rules (clause 5): fill every field of the form accurately; incomplete or erroneous applications are cancelled. t: Disciplinary & Grievance Policy: discharge, dismissal and misconduct
b:
Version 1.0, owner HR, effective 22 April 2021. If any clause conflicts with the Bangladesh Labour Act 2006 or Labour Rules 2015, the Act and Rules prevail.
Discharge (clause 4): an employee may be discharged for physical or mental incapacity or continued ill health only if certified in writing by a registered physician. Either side may have the report re-examined by a specialist not below Assistant Professor rank of a government medical college, at their own cost, within 10 days of receiving the certificate.
Dismissal (clause 5): at the Employer's discretion, an employee convicted of a criminal offence or found guilty of misconduct may be dismissed. Dismissal cannot be challenged for lack of prior notice or payment in lieu of notice.
Misconduct (5.3): wilful insubordination or disobedience to a lawful order; theft, misappropriation, fraud or dishonesty; taking or giving bribes or illegal gratification; habitual late attendance or habitual absence; absence without leave for more than 10 days; habitual breach of law, rules or regulations; disorderliness, riot, arson or breakage; habitual negligence of work; habitual breach of employment rules including conduct or discipline; altering, forging or damaging official records; any act against the peace, order and interest of the company, society and state (including attempts).
Alternative punishments (5.4): transfer to a lower post, grade or pay scale for up to 1 year; stoppage of promotion for up to 1 year; withholding of increment for up to 1 year; fine; suspension without wages for up to 7 days; censure and warning.
src: HR Policy: Disciplinary & Grievance Management Policy (v1.0, effective 22 Apr 2021)

t: Disciplinary & Grievance Policy: committee, procedure, investigation and appeal
b:
Committee (6): the Managing Director, or the Head of HR as authorized by the MD, forms a Disciplinary and Grievance Management Committee; proceedings are recorded in writing, and no employee of the accused's department can sit on it.
Procedure (7): the Committee may act on its own or on a written complaint if there are reasonable and objective grounds. The allegation is recorded in writing and the accused gets a copy with at least 7 days to explain, in writing or orally (oral explanations are recorded and signed). The Committee must avoid any coercion or intimidation. If the explanation is satisfactory, the accused is released by a written order and reinstated as if no allegation was made. Otherwise the Committee may form an Enquiry Team, then sends the report with observations and a proposed action to the Managing Director (optionally getting the accused's HOD's feedback first); action is taken in writing on the MD's approval. If the allegation is not proved, the accused is discharged of it by written order with the MD's approval.
Suspension during investigation: not more than 60 days; deemed on duty and paid half of basic and full other allowances; if found not guilty the deducted basic is returned in the next month's salary.
If an accused refuses a notice, it is treated as delivered if displayed on the notice board or sent by registered post. In awarding punishment, the employer may consider the previous record, gravity, contribution during service and special circumstances.
Enquiry Team (8): at least 3 members, not below the rank of the accused and not from the accused's team; completes within the time set by the Committee, not more than 60 days (extension possible with valid reason); the accused may defend, bring witnesses, and cross-examine; the team does not recommend punishment; the accused answers a written questionnaire.
Appeal (9): an aggrieved employee may apply to the Managing Director for review within 7 days of the order; it is disposed of within 30 days of receipt.

t: What counts as misconduct at Fiber@Home?
b: Insubordination, theft or fraud, bribery, habitual lateness or absence, absence without leave for more than 10 days, habitual breach of rules, riot or breakage, habitual negligence, forging or damaging official records, and acts against the interest of the company, society or state. Penalties range from censure and fine to demotion, stopped promotion or increment (up to 1 year), unpaid suspension up to 7 days, and dismissal.

t: How long do I have to respond to a disciplinary allegation and how can I appeal?
b: You get a written copy of the allegation and at least 7 days to explain. After an order, you can apply to the Managing Director for review within 7 days, and the review is decided within 30 days.

t: Can I be suspended during an investigation and is my salary cut?
b: Yes, for not more than 60 days. You are treated as on duty and paid half of basic salary and all other allowances. If found not guilty, the deducted basic is returned with the next month's salary.

t: How long can an investigation take?
b: The Enquiry Team (at least 3 members, not below the accused's rank) completes it within the time set by the Committee, not more than 60 days, unless an extension is requested with a valid reason. The team does not recommend punishment.

t: How do grievance and disciplinary complaints get raised?
b: The Disciplinary and Grievance Management Committee, formed by the MD or the Head of HR, can start action by itself or on a written complaint from any employee or person. The department raises an Investigation Request Form (complaint details, recommended by HOF, approved by HOD, then processed by HR).

t: IT Equipment Damage Management Policy: responsibilities and compensation
b:
Version 01, owner HR, effective 1 September 2018; applies to all employees for laptops, desktops and other IT equipment.
Employee (2.1): solely responsible for the safe and professional use of the equipment. Taking it outside the office compound in a business emergency needs consent of the HOD or HOF. Damage: notify the IT team immediately. Loss or embezzlement: notify the line manager immediately with a General Diary (GD) or First Information Report (FIR) copy from the nearest police station; the line manager informs IT, HR and Admin.
IT team (2.2): on a damage complaint, acknowledge, identify the likely cause and notify the employee and reporting line. If the employee is found negligent, IT shares a report with the loss calculation with HR within one week. If the employee disagrees, IT shares the report with the line manager for action, who sends it to HR. On a loss, IT blocks access, deactivates accounts and confirms the book value with Finance.
HR (2.3): forms an investigation committee, prepares a report and takes management approval. For damage, HR shares IT's feedback and the employee compensates the repair cost. For loss or embezzlement, an employee found guilty compensates 100% of the equipment's book value over a maximum of 12 months, deducted from monthly salary. Other disciplinary action by management can also apply. The overall investigation is completed within 60 days (maximum). Violations are a breach of the code of conduct leading to disciplinary action.
src: HR Policy: IT Equipment Damage Management Policy (v01, effective 1 Sep 2018)

t: What if I lose or damage my company laptop?
b: Damage: tell the IT team immediately; if negligence is found, you compensate the repair cost. Loss or theft: inform your line manager immediately with a GD or FIR copy from the nearest police station. If found guilty, you pay 100% of the equipment's book value, up to 12 months of salary deductions. Investigations finish within 60 days at most.
src: HR Policy: IT Equipment Damage Management Policy (v01, effective 1 Sep 2018)

t: Can I take my office laptop outside the office?
b: Only with the consent of your HOD or HOF, in a business emergency. You are solely responsible for the equipment's safety.
